message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may hold a maximum of **one month’s rent** (or two if the lease is for a month‑to‑month tenancy).
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds part of the deposit. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (e.g., functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control).
• Repairs that affect health or safety must be made promptly. | • Notify the landlord in writing (email or certified mail) of needed repairs.
• If the landlord fails to act, you may file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA) or seek a court order. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are reasonable (usually not more than 5% of the rent). | • Keep receipts or bank records of payments.
• If you’re late, communicate with the landlord and negotiate a payment plan if needed. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • You have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants.
• The landlord cannot enter your unit without **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) unless it’s an emergency. | • Document any unauthorized entries.
• If the landlord repeatedly violates this right, you can seek a restraining order or file a lawsuit. | | **Privacy** | • The landlord must respect your privacy and cannot conduct searches without a warrant or your consent, except in emergencies. | • If you suspect a warrantless search, consult an attorney. | | **Discrimination** | • Texas law (and federal Fair Housing Act) prohibits discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income. | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Lease Termination** | • For month‑to‑month leases, either party may terminate with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord may terminate early only for cause (e.g., nonpayment, violation of lease). | • Provide written notice and keep copies. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may **deduct the cost** from your rent (up to the amount of the repair) and pay the landlord the difference. | • Keep receipts and provide the landlord with a written notice of the deduction. | | **Eviction Process** | • The landlord must follow the Texas eviction procedure: serve a **Notice to Pay Rent or Quit** (3 days for nonpayment) or a **Notice to Cure or Quit** (10 days for lease violations).
• If you fail to comply, the landlord can file an unlawful detainer action. | • Respond promptly to notices.
• If you believe the eviction is unlawful, file a defense in court. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas offers free or low‑cost legal aid for tenants (e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, local bar association referral services). | • Contact a local tenant advocacy group or legal aid office for help. | #### Quick Tips 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of the lease, move‑in inspection, repair requests, and any communication with the landlord. 2. **Know the Timeline** – Texas has strict deadlines for notice and deposit returns; missing a deadline can cost you. 3. **Seek Mediation First** – Many disputes can be resolved through mediation before going to court. 4. **Know Your Local Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protections beyond state law. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific situations, consult a licensed attorney or a local tenant advocacy organization.
